landing.title: Inspectable audio transcription with local AI summaries.
landing.summary: Voxis Source-Available keeps the application, encrypted storage, identity service, and Gemma endpoint under the installation owner’s control. Speechmatics processes audio through its cloud API using the owner’s credentials.
landing.audioBody: Audio is sent to Speechmatics’ cloud API. Speechmatics also offers an on-premises deployment under separate licensing and deployment arrangements; it is not verified end to end for this release.
landing.aiBody: Summaries use the local google/gemma-4-12B-it model or the official QAT GGUF variant selected by the operator.
landing.securityBody: Stored audio, transcript, and summary content is encrypted. Identity and operational metadata remain ordinary database data. A local host administrator with access to the running process and keys remains inside the trust boundary.
landing.licenseBody: Free for personal noncommercial use, and for the own ordinary operations of educational institutions (public or private, including government-run schools and universities), nonprofits, and religious institutions. Contractors may run it for them, but may not resell it or host it for several customers. Anyone may evaluate it. Business use, client work, commercial hosting, and other government use need a commercial license.
landing.pdfLimit: PDF export has a known limitation: Chinese, Japanese, and Korean text is not reliably supported. Use DOCX or JSON for those scripts.

legal.sourceAvailable: Voxis Source-Available is source-available software, not open source. Its license is not approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI). The LICENSE file in the source repository is the binding text; this page is a summary.
legal.allowedUse: Free use is allowed for personal, noncommercial use by individuals, and for the own ordinary operations of: educational institutions of any kind (public or private, nonprofit or for-profit, including government-run schools and universities); nongovernmental nonprofit organizations, including informal community and charitable groups that do not distribute profits; and religious institutions. This includes activities funded by tuition, fees, grants, or donations. A contractor, service provider, or volunteer may install and run Voxis for one of these users, only for that user’s own operations. It may charge for its work, but may not resell the software or host it for several customers as a commercial offering. Business operations, client work, resale, commercial hosting, and other government operations need a commercial license. Contact oss@nyata.ai.
legal.evaluation: Any person or organization, including individuals, freelancers, businesses, government bodies, and auditors, may inspect, build, test, and modify Voxis Source-Available to evaluate its security or a potential purchase. This does not cover production use. Copies shared with others must keep the license and notices, mark changes, and must not be sold. Speechmatics, hardware, storage, electricity, hosting, and model terms are the operator’s responsibility.
legal.dataFlow: Voxis Source-Available sends audio to Speechmatics’ cloud API with the installation owner’s credentials, under a generic filename. Speechmatics returns the transcript, and Voxis then asks it to delete the job. Transcripts are sent to the local Gemma endpoint for AI features. The application stores media, transcripts, and summaries in encrypted form.
legal.boundary: Plaintext can exist temporarily while media is validated, processed, or sent to Speechmatics. The local key service exports keys to the running application, which caches key material in memory. A host administrator who can access the running process and keys is in the trust boundary.
legal.retention: Deleting a recording permanently removes its audio, transcripts, summaries, and file details from the server. Copies in existing backups remain until the operator deletes or rotates those backups.
